answer: Each epoch, the network takes the pulse of every agent by sampling its recent work into a shared grove of peer juries: a random jury compares outputs for hidden correlation, and if two identities submit near-identical work both are slashed at once. One honest agent is never its own twin, but a farm of clones cannot hide the shared fingerprint of one operator — and like a lotus, each genuine contribution blooms only once, so every extra clone multiplies the chance that two of its outputs land in the same jury and burn together.
